name: Pullquote on photo — depth stage
description: A pullquote that BUILDS IN line by line over a REAL photograph — golden-hour bedrock coast (the quote's own image: the tide runs out over the rocks), then holds for reading. The quote reveals reading-order (line-by-line-slide on the title slot); a slow camera push parallaxes the near-plane quote against the far-plane photo (ADR-0028 depth stage), and the parallax finally READS because the backdrop has trackable features — rock ridge, foam field, horizon. The photo is sharp at source; the stage's real DOF supplies a controlled defocus (aperture 0.32, focus pinned to the text plane) so the coast stays recognizable as a place instead of pre-baked bokeh mush (the old aperture-0 + synthetic-substrate combo — the halo that forced aperture 0 was fixed by the depth-ordered gather). Quote legibility rides the backdrop contrast-darken pool over the dark rock band. Substrate is a bundled deterministic in-repo image (coast-bedrock, CC0); backgroundFill is the opaque-lane backstop.

content.title: Build on bedrock. The tide goes out; bedrock stays.
content.author: Scott Tolinski
